- When sentiment is high (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and price is falling, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates early in 30-day horizon; apply 1–2% upward bias for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment swings from high to low, model lags in adjusting; delay forecast correction by 1–2 days if sentiment drops sharply.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, model often fails to recognize it; apply 1–3% upward adjustment to counteract downward drift.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in 10–20 day horizon; use 3-period weighted average for mid-term correction.
